title: Automated Legacy Code Refactoring Pipeline
business: Enterprise software maintenance teams managing massive, undocumented legacy codebases.
problem: Manual refactoring of legacy modules is error-prone, time-consuming, and often introduces regressions due to lack of context and complex dependency chains.
solution: Utilize GPT-5.1 with configurable reasoning effort to analyze legacy code structures and generate refactored patches, leveraging its specialized coding capabilities to ensure logical consistency across modular boundaries.
steps: Ingest legacy source files into the context window using the Chat Completions API.
Configure the reasoning_effort parameter to 'high' to allow the model to deeply evaluate dependency impacts before proposing changes.
Utilize the apply_patch tool to programmatically implement refactoring suggestions directly into the codebase.
Validate the output through automated regression suites to ensure the model-generated logic maintains original functionality.
outcome: A more maintainable codebase with reduced technical debt and fewer human-introduced bugs during the refactoring process.
limitation: High reasoning effort increases latency and token consumption; developers must monitor the ratio of reasoning tokens to output quality to ensure cost-efficiency.
